No textbook is required. The references below support the lessons; lesson files and tutorials are linked from each class page.

### Reading

- Wassily Kandinsky, Point and Line to Plane — conceptual reference for geometry and graphic relationships.
- Robert Woodbury, Elements of Parametric Design — relationships, dependencies and change.
- Casey Reas, Chandler McWilliams and LUST, Form+Code — repetition, transformation and visualization.
- Arturo Tedeschi, AAD Algorithms-Aided Design — an additional Grasshopper reference where that environment is supported.
- Diego García Cuevas and Gianluca Pugliese, Advanced 3D Printing with Grasshopper: Clay and FDM — fabrication and toolpath reference.
- Anthony Di Mari and Nora Yoo, Operative Design: A Catalog of Spatial Verbs — the CSG operations named as spatial acts; primary reference for the massing sequence.
- Anthony Di Mari, Conditional Design: An Introduction to Elemental Architecture — the companion volume; operations driven by a condition or rule.
- Neil Spiller, Drawing Architecture; Peter Cook, Drawing: The Motive Force of Architecture — architectural drawing and visual communication.

### Example graphic standards manuals

Shown in Class 01 and the reference for the Graphic Standards Manual. Each is a page grid, a type hierarchy and a rule for every case that comes up. Read them for how much of each one is rules rather than pictures.

| Manual | What to look for |
| --- | --- |
| [NYCTA Graphics Standards Manual (1970)](https://archive.org/details/nycta-gs-manual) | Massimo Vignelli and Bob Noorda, Unimark International. A binder of cases: every sign in the New York subway drawn at size with its rule beside it. Full scan. |
| [NASA Graphics Standards Manual (1975, NHB 1430-2)](https://archive.org/details/NASA_Graphics_Standards_Manual) | Richard Danne and Bruce Blackburn. One mark, and a hundred pages of where it is allowed to go. What is designed is the consistency. Full scan, public domain. |
| [Munich 1972 — visual design guidelines](https://www.otlaicher.de/en/articles/the-rainbow-games/) | Otl Aicher, 1967–1972. A grid, a fixed set of angles and one component varied across a whole field of pictograms. A restricted palette held for four years. |

### Generative design (Project 4)

| Reference | Use |
| --- | --- |
| [Morphogenesis resources (Jason Webb)](https://github.com/jasonwebb/morphogenesis-resources) | Project 4: one page per strategy (differential growth, DLA, reaction-diffusion, cellular automata, agents, physics), with pictures, papers and code. |
| [The Nature of Code (Daniel Shiffman)](https://natureofcode.com/) | Project 4: random and noise, forces, agents and steering, cellular automata, fractals and evolution, explained with running examples. |
| [Museum of Emotions competition results (Buildner)](https://www.archdaily.com/1032328) | Project 4.3: the level of drawing quality, post-processing and storytelling we are looking for on the competition sheet. |
| [The Last Nuclear Bomb Memorial competition results (Buildner)](https://www.archdaily.com/1041457) | Project 4.3: a second set of competition sheets to study for hierarchy, colour and annotation. |
| [Parametric Camp (Jose Luis Garcia del Castillo y Lopez)](https://www.youtube.com/@ParametricCamp) | Computational design videos; start with the Introduction to Parametric Modeling with Grasshopper playlist. |
| [Grasshopper plugins for Project 4](https://www.food4rhino.com/) | Rabbit (cellular automata, L-systems), Culebra (agents), Anemone (loops), Kangaroo (physics). Credit any plugin you use. |

### Technical documentation

- [BIG-style process diagram tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Y5Rn3bDL5s) — CSG 2.1: reference for the operation sequence and graphic presentation.
- [Three-point lighting tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RDbrOpnIY7Q) — Module 3.1: reference for one consistent key, fill and rim/back lighting strategy across three panel variations.
- [Blender Repeat Zone](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/modeling/geometry_nodes/utilities/repeat_zone.html) — Explicit iteration with Repeat Input and Repeat Output.
- [Blender 5.2 manual](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/index.html) — Check exact node behavior against the version used to prepare the lesson.
